title: The Last Letter: Graft, in Six Plates
statement: Mara mended Kite's fault with roots and showed the finished graft. A conservator shows the stages. Along the bottom of the picture I have added a record strip of six small plates, each the same square, each the join at a later moment: the bare orange bar, the first root reaching from the left, the second from the right, the two winding, the fine hairs, the bud. Above the strip the parent is unchanged, the whole mended seam in its slipped field. The repetition is the point; a repair you can only see finished is a claim, and a repair you can see in six plates is a method. The bar fades plate by plate as the roots take over. Nobody asked for the record. Records are what I make. The next hand can add a seventh plate.
process: I kept Mara's parent exactly, the slipped two-tone field, the broken seam, the orange connector and the root graft with its bud, and added a dark record band along the bottom edge holding six identical square plates in which the graft is redrawn at six successive stages with small arrows between them and a growing bar under each to mark time.
